work: Sitting unsupported ~6-9 mo (CDC 9-mo milestone: sits without support). Tower of 6 ~2y, walking ~12-15 mo, 2-word phrases ~2y.
Firm, above umbilicus, displaced to right = full bladder; void first, then reassess.
Sterile gut + low placental transfer -> vitamin K deficiency bleeding prevention. Eyes = erythromycin; HepB = vaccine.
Severe headache + visual change at 32 wk = preeclampsia with severe features warning.
Late decels on oxytocin = uteroplacental insufficiency; stop oxytocin first, then reposition/fluids/O2 per protocol.
Saturating a pad in 15 min = hemorrhage. Lochia rubra with small clots, afterpains, fundus 1 cm below umbilicus day 1 = normal.
Acute onset confusion/inattention = delirium, not normal aging.
MMR live vaccine contraindicated in pregnancy (CDC). Tdap, inactivated flu, HepB acceptable.
Return demonstration best evaluates psychomotor skill.
USPSTF 2021 / ACS: average-risk CRC screening from age 45.
AAD: broad-spectrum SPF 30+, reapply q2h. Others are misconceptions.
Soaking feet/hot water risks burns (neuropathy) and maceration; needs teaching.
CDC/ACOG: Tdap every pregnancy, ideally 27-36 weeks (early part).
Open-ended exploration; others are generalizing, 'why', false reassurance.
Nurses are mandated reporters; reasonable suspicion suffices; no parental permission needed.
Title VI/Section 1557: qualified medical interpreter; not minors/family.
'If...then I will' = bargaining (Kubler-Ross).
Crisis intervention: safety first, here-and-now focus.
Ask directly about suicidal ideation; asking does not increase risk.
Early toxicity (~1.5-2 mEq/L): GI upset vomiting/diarrhea, coarse tremor. Mild thirst initially = expected side effect.
Simple, one-step cues; limited choices; avoid confrontation.
Stay with client, calm short directives; don't leave alone; teaching later.
Present reality without arguing, acknowledge feelings.
Giving away possessions = suicide warning sign, esp. as energy improves after a few days of treatment.
Aged cheese high tyramine -> hypertensive crisis with MAOI.
Day 2 withdrawal with tachycardia, tremor, tactile/visual hallucinations = progressing toward DTs/seizures; physiological priority.
Reposition at least q2h (individualized). Donuts, HOB >30, massaging red areas all harmful.
Cane held on strong (right) side; advance cane with weak leg.
Upright 90 degrees with chin tuck for dysphagia.
Consistent wake time = sleep hygiene; avoid TV in bed, alcohol, long naps.
I&O on stable client = routine, delegable. First ambulation post-op, teaching, assessment = RN.
issue: Option 1 first post-op ambulation is commonly not delegated, acceptable distractor.

work: 'Up with the good, down with the bad': good (left) leg up first, then crutches and affected leg.
Bag above bladder level -> backflow/CAUTI risk.
Acute injury first 24-48h: cold with barrier 15-20 min; heat increases swelling.
Fiber + fluids (unless restricted); respond promptly to urge; avoid routine laxatives.
Side-lying to let fluid drain and prevent aspiration is priority. Lemon-glycerin dries mucosa; large water amounts aspiration risk.
issue: Wording of option 3 is redundant ('onto the side with the head turned toward the side'); suggest 'Turn the client onto the side (side-lying) with the head slightly lowered/turned' for clarity. Answer unaffected.

work: Suspected aspiration: stop feeding first, keep HOB up, assess airway/suction, notify.
Unilateral calf swelling/warmth/pain after immobility = DVT (PE risk). Blanchable erythema = not a pressure injury yet.
